title: smsR: A seasonal assessment model for exploited stocks
content:
We present a seasonal age-based stock assessment model implemented in R, enabling stochastic estimation within the Template Model Builder framework for efficient parameter estimation and random effects modelling. Applied as the official model for several North Sea small pelagic stocks, the approach captures within-year variation in growth, mortality, and recruitment, and simulation analyses demonstrate reduced bias for stocks with strong seasonal dynamics. The accompanying software provides diagnostic, forecasting, and management strategy evaluation tools, illustrated through a full North Sea sandeel assessment as a practical application.


Abstract

We present a seasonal stock assessment model, which allows the user to initiate a stochastic age-based model inside the R programming language. The model is currently the official stock assessment model for five small pelagic stocks in the North Sea. The seasonality component enables within year changes in weight, natural mortality and recruitment, which is commonly missing from existing methods. We show through simulation analysis that including seasonality can lead to lower bias in stocks with strong interannual dynamics. We provide a variety of useful functions and applications that let the user perform diagnostics and evaluate the goodness-of-fit of the model. The software contains functions used for catch forecasting and management strategy evaluation. The stock assessment model is written in Template Model Builder (TMB), which enables rapid parameter estimation and the potential to estimate parameters as random effects. Practical implication. The model offers a tool for consistent and transparent stock assessments for populations with strong seasonal dynamics.
